annotations.title: List Standards in a Blueprint Category

description:
List every standard a Georgia Milestones test assesses under one blueprint claim (a reporting category such as 'Numerical Reasoning'), with point weights. This is the reverse of the per-standard coverage view. Pass an `assessment_id` (from list_assessments) and a `claim_code` (the category heading, e.g. 'Numerical Reasoning', or for ELA '<strand>.<domain>' like 'Texts.Interpreting Texts'); optionally narrow to one `target_text`. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces. Returns `standards` with `code`, `statement`, `claim_name`, `target_text`, `approx_points`, `sub_codes`, and `qualifier`.

READING THE POINTS. `approx_points` is the weight of a claim or target, never of one standard, and a blueprint often draws one merged points cell across several targets. Rows sharing a merged cell repeat that value and share a `points_group` id; each is flagged `points_shared: true`, names its co-covered codes in `points_shared_with`, and carries a ready-to-quote `approx_points_note`. Rows with different `points_group` ids are separate pools. So do not add up `approx_points` down the rows: use the precomputed `claim_total_points`, bounded by `assessment_total_points` / `design_total_points`. Worked example: grade 5 math Numerical Reasoning has 5 rows reading 14/14/14/10/10 (62 if summed), but 5.NR.1+5.NR.4 share one 14-point pool and 5.NR.2+5.NR.5 share one 10-point pool, so the claim is 38 points on a 58-point test. An unknown claim or assessment_id is an error that lists the valid values.

target_text.description: Optional target within the claim, as written in the blueprint.
